body.statement:
Suppose the feature dimension \(p\) is fixed and \(n\to\infty\).  For each fixed bulk coordinate \(k\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\), the coordinate influences of the empirical gradient at \(\beta=0\) for true-propensity IPW, exact entropy-balanced IPW, and oracle DR are respectively
\[
 \psi_{T,k}=\tfrac12SYq_k,qquad
 \psi_{E,k}=\tfrac12S\bigl[\{Y-\tfrac12\}q_k-\mu_k\bigr],
 \qquad
 \psi_{D,k}=\tfrac12S\{Y-m(q)\}q_k,
\]
where \(\mu=\mathbb E\{m(q)q\}\) and \(\mu_k=0\) for \(k>1\).  Their variances are
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{T,k})=\frac18,qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})=\frac1{16},qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{D,k})=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\to1\) in this fixed-dimensional regime.
body.proof_tex:
At \(\beta=0\), \(\sigma'(0)=1/4\) and \(h'(0)=0\).  Therefore one observation contributes \(\psi_T=SYq/2\) to the true-IPW gradient and \(\psi_D=S(Y-m(q))q/2\) to the oracle-DR gradient.  For a bulk coordinate \(k>1\), \(q_k\) is independent of \(q_1\), \(\mathbb E m(q)=1/2\) by \(m(-q_1)=1-m(q_1)\), and randomization makes \(S\) conditionally mean zero.  Hence both influences have mean zero and
\[
 \mathbb E\psi_{T,k}^2
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E(Yq_k^2)=\tfrac18,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\psi_{D,k}^2
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E[m(q)\{1-m(q)\}q_k^2]=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]

For entropy balancing, let \(\bar q_a\) and \(\overline{Yq}_a\) denote the unweighted arm means.  At zero tilt, the derivative of the exponentially tilted arm mean of \(q\) is its sample covariance, which converges to \(I_p\).  A fixed-dimensional Taylor expansion of the exact balance equation therefore gives
\[
 \eta_{an}=\bar q_n-\bar q_a+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Let \(M_a=\sum_{i:A_{ni}=a}w_{ian}Y_{ni}q_{ni}\).  The derivative at zero tilt of the corresponding weighted mean of \(Yq\) is
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Yq,q)
 =\mathbb E\{m(q)qq^{\top}\}=\tfrac12I_p.
\]
The last equality follows by pairing \(q_1\) with \(-q_1\): \(qq^{\top}\) is unchanged for diagonal and off-signal bulk entries, the remaining odd cross entries integrate to zero, and \(m(q_1)+m(-q_1)=1\).  Thus
\[
 M_a-\mu=\overline{Yq}_a-\mu+  frac12(\bar q_n-\bar q_a)+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
For any square-integrable vector \(f\) with mean \(\nu\), the arm ratio obeys the direct expansion
\[
 \frac{\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)f\}}{\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)\}}-\nu
 =2\mathbb P_n[\mathbf1(A=a)(f-\nu)]+o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
because \(\mathbb P_n\{\mathbf1(A=a)\}=1/2+O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) and the centered numerator is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\).  Applying this identity to the two sample means shows that the one-observation influence of \(M_a\) is
\[
 2\mathbf1\{A=a\}(Yq-\mu)+  frac12\{q-2\mathbf1\{A=a\}q\}.
\]
The entropy-balanced gradient is \((M_1-M_0)/4\).  Subtracting the two arm influences and using \(S=2A-1\) gives
\[
 \psi_E=\tfrac12S\bigl[\{Y-  frac12\}q-\mu\bigr].
\]
Symmetry gives \(\mu_k=0\) for \(k>1\).  Since a binary \(Y\) obeys \((Y-1/2)^2=1/4\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})
 =\tfrac14\mathbb E[\{Y-  frac12\}^2q_k^2]=\frac1{16}.
\]

For completeness, fixed-dimensional strict feasibility follows directly from full support of the Gaussian law.  Choose \(p+1\) deterministic vertices whose simplex contains a neighborhood of zero.  Small neighborhoods of those vertices retain this property and each has positive probability in each randomized arm.  With probability tending to one every such neighborhood is represented in both arms; simultaneously \(\bar q_n\to0\), so \(\bar q_n\) lies in the interior of each arm hull.  Gaussian absolute continuity also gives \(\operatorname{rank}(Q_n)=p\) almost surely once \(n\ge p\).  This proves the event assertion and validates the tilt expansions on an event whose probability tends to one.
